dossiers.title: Kaplansky zero-divisor conjecture: bounded post-Gardam audit
dossiers.formulation: For a specified torsion-free group G and an integral domain R, decide whether the explicitly supplied nonzero elements of R[G] multiply to zero. The general zero-divisor formulation is kept distinct from Kaplansky's unit conjecture.
dossiers.scope: A finite group-presentation and group-ring computation audit, with coefficient ring, normal forms, and support convention fixed before work starts.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not infer a zero divisor from a nontrivial unit, does not generalize a characteristic-specific construction, and does not state the global status of the conjecture.
dossiers.motivation: Post-Gardam work is a useful guardrail against conflating adjacent group-ring conjectures and against treating a reproducible finite product as a theorem about all torsion-free groups.
dossiers.falsifier: The bounded claim fails if the group is not established torsion-free under the supplied presentation, either supplied element is zero, or their product does not reduce to zero in the declared ring.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A bounded audit settles only its named multiplication statement. Any general conclusion requires an external group theorist's review of hypotheses, coefficient ring, and logical implication.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: no sentence here asserts a current global resolution or non-resolution of Kaplansky's zero-divisor conjecture.
dossiers.safety: Use public presentations and reproducible algebra only; do not substitute model memory for a cited group-theoretic implication.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: A group theorist independent of the artifact author must check the presentation, torsion-free premise, and ring convention; a second reviewer must check the distinction between unit and zero-divisor statements.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck post-Gardam literature and the exact named conjecture before publishing any status language.

variant_distinctions.distinction: A nontrivial unit and a zero divisor answer different assertions; neither is silently substituted for the other.
The coefficient field or integral domain is part of the statement; a result in one characteristic is not a result in another without a cited transfer theorem.

bounded_subgoals.question: Reproduce one named finite group-ring multiplication in the coefficient ring specified by the source.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: Normal-form reduction yields a nonzero product or an element is not represented as claimed.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One presentation and one coefficient ring only; no global conjecture claim.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Versioned presentation, reduction trace, independent CAS rerun, and source locator table.

references.locator: Abstract and Conjecture 1; distinguish the zero-divisor formulation from adjacent conjectures.

dossiers.title: Union-closed families: post-Gilmer bounded constant audit
dossiers.formulation: For a finite nontrivial union-closed family F, test a stated lower-bound claim about the maximum element frequency using the exact family encoding and denominator convention supplied by the artifact.
dossiers.scope: Finite-family certificates, exact frequency calculations, and source mapping for a stated constant lower bound.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not assert Frankl's one-half conclusion, improve any constant, or treat a preprint claim as accepted merely because it has a numerical bound.
dossiers.motivation: This problem rewards careful separation between a conjectured one-half threshold, a proved positive constant, and a finite computation that can actually fail.
dossiers.falsifier: The bounded statement fails if the family is not union-closed, the denominator differs from the declared convention, or every element falls below the claimed bound.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A checked family or source theorem settles only the named finite or cited assertion; external combinatorics review is required for any transfer to a broader class.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: this source makes no current-status assertion about the union-closed sets conjecture or the best known constant.
dossiers.safety: Retain exact finite inputs and arithmetic; do not report approximate frequency output as a proof.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: An independent extremal-combinatorics reviewer must check the union-closure convention and theorem anchor; a second reviewer must audit any claimed reduction.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck the primary literature for subsequent improvements before a public statement names any bound.

variant_distinctions.variant: One-half conjecture versus constant lower bound
variant_distinctions.distinction: A positive constant lower bound is not the one-half conclusion and must be labeled with its own quantified statement.
An exhaustive computation over an encoded finite family does not become a theorem over all union-closed families.

bounded_subgoals.question: Verify union closure and exact element frequencies for one supplied finite family, then compare them with one explicitly stated bound.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: A union is absent, parsing changes the family, or the computed maximum frequency misses the bound.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One finite family and one named bound only; no global proof claim.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Canonical family encoding, exact rational frequency table, and independently rerun verifier.

references.locator: Abstract and main theorem statement giving the 0.01 constant in the stated setting.
references.why_here: Primary anchor for a bounded constant, not a current-status assertion.

dossiers.title: Erdős–Straus: reproducible finite-range decomposition program
dossiers.formulation: For each integer n in an explicitly declared finite interval with n >= 2, find or verify positive integers x, y, z satisfying 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z.
dossiers.scope: A deterministic finite interval, exact rational arithmetic, reproducible decompositions, and explicit treatment of every n in that interval.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not claim the universal conjecture from a finite range, does not accept floating-point equality, and does not silently restrict to primes or congruence classes.
dossiers.motivation: The problem is ideal for a detection-floor discipline: a range certificate is valuable precisely when it says what it did not cover.
dossiers.falsifier: The bounded claim fails if any n in the declared interval has no supplied exact decomposition or if a purported identity fails after cross multiplication.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A successful run settles only the stated interval and algorithm version. Any universal theorem needs an independent number theorist's proof review.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: this is a finite verification design, not a claim about the current resolution status of the Erdős–Straus conjecture.
dossiers.safety: Store exact integers and deterministic seeds; no performance estimate or sampled search may be presented as coverage.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: An independent number theorist must review the formulation and interval reduction; a separate reviewer must rerun the exact arithmetic verifier.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck existing verification ranges and theorem claims before publishing a comparison.

variant_distinctions.distinction: Coverage up to a declared endpoint is bounded evidence, not a proof for every n.

variant_distinctions.variant: Exact rational identity versus numerical approximation
variant_distinctions.distinction: The denominator identity is checked by integers; floating-point agreement is not an accepted witness.

bounded_subgoals.question: Produce a complete certificate for 2 <= n <= N where N is committed in the artifact manifest before execution.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: One uncovered n, a nonpositive denominator, or a failed integer cross-product check.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: The fixed manifest range only; no extrapolation beyond N.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Sorted decomposition table, exact verifier, coverage count, and independent replay log.

dossiers.title: Sums of three cubes: fixed-n artifact verification
dossiers.formulation: For one explicitly named integer k that is not excluded by the stated congruence obstruction, verify a supplied integer triple (x, y, z) satisfying x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = k, or record a bounded search with a declared search region and no conclusion outside it.
dossiers.scope: Exact integer witnesses, congruence filters, bounded searches, and source anchors for a selected k.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not list supposedly outstanding k values, infer nonexistence from search exhaustion outside its certified domain, or announce a general solution.
dossiers.motivation: This slate item tests artifact provenance: an enormous integer witness is easy to display but still needs an exact verifier and a sharply stated search boundary.
dossiers.falsifier: A witness claim fails if exact cubing does not return k; a bounded-search claim fails if its enumerator omits a declared region or its congruence filter is wrong.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A verified triple settles only its chosen k. A no-witness result remains a bounded negative result unless a proof independently establishes nonexistence.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: no live list of outstanding integers and no current-status claim are asserted here.
dossiers.safety: Use checked big-integer arithmetic and publish the code and bounds; no unverified distributed-compute report is evidence.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: An independent computational number theorist must check the congruence condition and search boundary; a second reviewer must run the verifier from the artifact manifest.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck the selected k and source record immediately before public wording refers to an outstanding case.

variant_distinctions.distinction: An exact triple is a witness for one k; exhausting a bounded region is not a nonexistence proof.
A modular obstruction and a case not eliminated by that obstruction are not the same logical classification.

bounded_subgoals.question: Verify one supplied triple for one declared k with arbitrary-precision arithmetic and independent implementation agreement.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: Exact evaluation differs from k or an input integer is altered by parsing.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One k and one witness only; no claim about other k values.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Canonical decimal inputs, two verifier outputs, and SHA-256 digests of the source artifact.

dossiers.title: Sendov: degree-indexed proof-claim audit
dossiers.formulation: For a monic or nonmonic polynomial p whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk, a selected root a is paired with a critical point c satisfying |a-c| <= 1, under the exact multiplicity and boundary conventions stated by the source being audited.
dossiers.scope: A degree-indexed audit of a named paper or finite polynomial family, including the source's precise root and critical-point conventions.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not treat an abstract assertion of a proof as settled, does not mix degree ranges, and does not replace exact root certification with a plotted approximation.
dossiers.motivation: A degree-aware audit turns a famous conjecture into falsifiable local checks while resisting the common mistake of treating a claimed complete proof as an already reviewed theorem.
dossiers.falsifier: A degree-specific claim fails if an allowed root lacks a certified critical point within the stated distance, or if the source's degree/radius hypotheses do not match the audited instance.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A completed audit approves only the explicitly reviewed degree range or source lemma. Full-resolution language requires independent complex-analysis review of a complete proof.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: this dossier makes no current-status assertion about Sendov's conjecture or any claimed proof.
dossiers.safety: Use interval or exact certification for numerical roots; label a floating-point exploration as exploratory only.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: Two independent complex analysts must review any degree-range conclusion, including one who checks the interpretation of multiple roots and the source's theorem scope.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck peer review, errata, and the exact degree range before any public description of progress.

variant_distinctions.distinction: A verified degree range is not a proof for arbitrary degree.
A plotted critical point is not a certificate that the required distance inequality holds.

bounded_subgoals.question: For a finite source-supplied polynomial family of one declared degree, certify the root-to-critical-point distance inequalities.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: An interval enclosure excludes all critical points within distance one for an allowed root.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: The named family and degree only; no all-degree conclusion.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Polynomial list, certified root enclosures, critical-point enclosures, and independent checker output.

references.why_here: Primary author-withdrawal record and original claimed-proof anchor; the dossier uses it only to guard against converting a claim into a theorem.

dossiers.title: Lonely runner: explicit small-k certificate program
dossiers.formulation: For a declared nonzero integer velocity vector (u_1, ..., u_k), find or verify a time t satisfying ||t u_i|| >= 1/(k+1) for every i, with the norm and runner-count convention fixed by the source.
dossiers.scope: Exact finite velocity instances, a declared small k, and certificates with rational or rigorously enclosed times.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not convert a checked instance into the general lonely-runner conjecture and does not quote a largest proven k without a pre-publication source refresh.
dossiers.motivation: The small-k program is well suited to reviewable certificates, provided the runner-count convention is made explicit and no finite verification is inflated into a general theorem.
dossiers.falsifier: The certificate fails if any declared velocity has distance below the threshold at the supplied time or if the stated k convention changes the threshold.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A valid certificate settles one velocity vector. Any theorem for a k range requires an independent combinatorics or discrete-geometry review.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: no sentence here reports a current best k or a current global status of the lonely runner conjecture.
dossiers.safety: Use exact modular arithmetic or validated intervals; do not certify a threshold from a rounded plot.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: An independent specialist must check the k convention and threshold; a second reviewer must reproduce the certificate arithmetic.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck current computer-assisted and proof literature before publishing any small-k comparison.

variant_distinctions.variant: Number of runners versus k parameter
variant_distinctions.distinction: The threshold depends on the stated convention; a source using k+1 runners is not silently relabeled as one using k runners.
A time witness for one velocity tuple is not a theorem for all tuples at that k.

bounded_subgoals.question: Verify a rational-time certificate for one supplied integer velocity tuple at one declared k.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: Exact distance-to-nearest-integer arithmetic violates the threshold for any velocity.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One velocity tuple only; no coverage claim for all tuples.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Velocity manifest, rational time witness, exact distance table, and independent rerun.

dossiers.title: Busy Beaver 6: model-fixed lower-bound artifact coordination
dossiers.formulation: For one transition table in the declared n-state, two-symbol, blank-tape Turing-machine model, verify that the machine halts after at least L steps. The precise Busy Beaver function name and transition convention are part of the statement.
dossiers.scope: One fixed machine model, one encoded six-state transition table, a trace/checker pair, and a lower-bound statement only.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not identify different Busy Beaver conventions, claim an exact BB(6) value, or accept a large decimal number without a checkable execution argument.
dossiers.motivation: Busy Beaver work makes provenance and formal checking decisive: a lower bound is useful only when another party can identify the exact machine model and verify the claimed halting behavior.
dossiers.falsifier: The lower-bound claim fails if the transition table is outside the declared model, the trace diverges, or the machine halts before L under the specified blank-tape convention.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A checked run establishes a lower bound for the fixed model and machine. Exact-value language requires an independently reviewed upper-bound classification in the same model.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: no current lower bound or exact status for BB(6) is asserted in this dossier.
dossiers.safety: Treat all huge-number claims as untrusted until a deterministic checker reproduces them; retain no hidden compute transcript as a substitute for the artifact.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: A computability specialist must verify the exact machine convention and reduction; an independent formal-methods reviewer must check any proof-assistant correspondence claim.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck the active BBChallenge record and model convention before publishing a numerical comparison.

variant_distinctions.distinction: A maximum halting-time convention and a maximum-ones convention are not interchangeable Busy Beaver quantities.
A witness machine proves only a lower bound until an upper-bound classification is independently established in the same model.

bounded_subgoals.question: Replay one supplied six-state transition table to a checkpointed lower-bound threshold using a deterministic, independently implemented checker.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: The encodings differ, the replay fails before the threshold, or the checker reports a different state/tape convention.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One machine and stated lower bound only; no exact BB(6) claim.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Transition-table string, checkpoint hashes, verifier source digest, and independent replay receipt.

references.locator: Definition of BB and machine-convention section: two symbols, state A, and an all-zero initial tape; no six-state record or exact-value claim is taken from this anchor.
references.why_here: Official convention anchor for model-fixed, checkable Busy Beaver artifacts; it replaces an unrelated five-state paper.

dossiers.title: Quantum channel additivity: finite-dimensional counterexample-hunt discipline
dossiers.formulation: For a fully specified finite-dimensional quantum channel or channel pair and a named information quantity, compare the declared one-use and two-use quantities using a validated optimization/certification method.
dossiers.scope: A named channel family, a named additivity functional, finite dimensions, and explicit numerical or analytic error bounds.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not use 'additivity' without naming the functional, does not infer a general statement from one numerical optimizer, and does not confuse a known counterexample family with every channel class.
dossiers.motivation: The historic additivity landscape has several non-equivalent quantities. A disciplined finite hunt can contribute a checkable example or negative result without collapsing those distinctions.
dossiers.falsifier: The candidate violation fails if the channel is not completely positive trace preserving, the stated functional is computed under inconsistent conventions, or certified error bars permit equality.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A certified finite example settles only its named inequality. Any general class statement requires independent quantum-information review and a proof matching the functional exactly.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: no current-status assertion is made for any general quantum-channel additivity question.
dossiers.safety: Document numerical conditioning and optimizer failure modes; never label an unconstrained numerical output a counterexample without certificate bounds.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: An independent quantum-information theorist must check the functional and channel conventions; a separate numerical reviewer must check certification and error analysis.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck the precise additivity property and known counterexamples before any public comparison.

variant_distinctions.distinction: Minimum-output entropy, Holevo capacity, and other additivity statements are separate mathematical claims.
An optimizer finding is exploratory until error bounds and channel validity certify the strict inequality.

bounded_subgoals.question: For one declared low-dimensional channel pair and one named functional, reproduce a source-supplied inequality with certified tolerance.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: The maps fail CPTP checks, the functional convention changes, or the certified interval contains equality.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One channel pair and one functional only; no statement about all channels.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Kraus or Choi data, CPTP checker, optimization settings, interval certificate, and independent rerun.

references.locator: Abstract and the named communication-capacity additivity claim; retain the functional exactly as stated.
references.why_here: Primary anchor for the distinction between an additivity question and a counterexample construction.

dossiers.title: Navier–Stokes: finite Galerkin energy-balance check
dossiers.formulation: For a specified divergence-free Fourier-Galerkin truncation of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equation on the periodic torus, verify the stated finite-dimensional energy identity or residual bound over a declared finite time interval.
dossiers.scope: A fixed truncation, viscosity, initial data, forcing convention, integrator/certificate, and finite time interval.
dossiers.out_of_scope: The dossier does not assert global regularity, finite-time singularity, convergence of a numerical scheme to a PDE solution, or any answer to the Clay problem.
dossiers.motivation: The flagship statement gate benefits from a deliberately bounded PDE task whose evidence can fail, while making the distance from a finite computation to a three-dimensional regularity theorem unmistakable.
dossiers.falsifier: The bounded claim fails if divergence freedom is violated beyond the declared certificate, the energy identity residual exceeds the stated bound, or the run uses different parameters than its manifest.
dossiers.settlement_conditions: A valid run settles only its finite truncation and interval. No numerical result can change the status language of the global existence-and-smoothness problem.
dossiers.no_resolution_language: Draft only: this is not a Navier–Stokes solution claim and it makes no current-status assertion about the Clay problem.
dossiers.safety: Treat simulations as bounded evidence; expose precision, residuals, and instability diagnostics rather than suggesting physical or mathematical proof.
dossiers.external_expert_requirements: An independent PDE analyst must check the truncation-to-PDE boundary and energy identity; a second reviewer must check the numerical certificate and parameter manifest.

status_freshness.recheck_instruction: Recheck the official formulation and any claimed developments before wording compares this task to the global problem.

variant_distinctions.distinction: A finite-dimensional truncation is not the full Navier–Stokes equation and cannot prove global regularity by itself.
The periodic and whole-space settings have separately stated hypotheses and are never merged in an artifact label.

bounded_subgoals.question: Check a specified energy balance for one periodic Fourier-Galerkin truncation over [0,T] with declared residual tolerance.
bounded_subgoals.falsifier: The residual certificate exceeds tolerance, divergence-free constraints fail, or a manifest parameter is missing.
bounded_subgoals.boundary: One finite truncation and time interval only; no PDE regularity conclusion.
bounded_subgoals.evidence_artifact: Mode manifest, solver version, interval or residual certificate, and independently rerun checker.

references.locator: Official problem description, alternatives (A)–(D) on pages 2–3; use it to preserve the global-problem boundary.
